newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end lower, yen, marks fall late.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end lower, yen, marks fall late.

text.p: Most IMM currencies ended slightly lower, with September yen and marks setting session lows late due to strength in the U.S. asset markets, traders and analysts said.
September yen fell to $0.008914, through support at $0.008924 or 113.50 spot marks, and September marks inched closer to support at $0.5790, or 1.7380 spot marks, late in lackluster trade.
The erosion in most key currencies coincided with the rally in the U.S. T-bond market, which helped lift the dollar to the upper end of ranges, they said.

"The supreme confidence in U.S. markets is helping the dollar," George Tzanetatos, vice president at Merrill Lynch, said. While U.S. stocks were softer on Wednesday, most indexes have set a string of record highs within the last week.
The strength in the U.S. asset market reflects the positive U.S. economic environment of strong growth and low inflation, they said.
The Federal Reserve's Beige Book summary based on information collected before June 9 said all 12 districts in the United States grew in May and early June, but there were pockets of weakness.
The data will be used by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) when they meet on July 1-2 to set monetary policy.
The currency futures market had little reaction to statements out of Germany. German finance minister Theo Waigel said the government would reach a compromise deal on the German budget.

Bundesbank council member Peter Schmidhuber said the European Central Bank was bound to uphold the stability of the euro after the start of the European currency union. German officials in general expressed relief that they were able to prevent efforts to weaken the euro at the Amsterdam summit.
Tzanetatos said uncertainties about the European monetary union (EMU), coupled with U.S.-Japan trade issues would dominate talks at the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Denver this weekend.
April U.S. international trade data will be released on Thursday at 0830 EDT/1330 GMT. The U.S. deficit is expected to wident to $10 billion, from $8.5 billion in March.
Tzanetatos said the dollar was preparing to rally out of its recent ranges, particularly against the mark.
"The consolidation will be shortly ending," he said. "You can feel it because the dollar finds buying on the lows."
Support for September marks is at $0.5784, or 1.74 spot, and at $0.5777, which currently corresponds to the June 6 high of 1.7420 spot. September's contract low is at $0.5770.

At the end of pit trade, September yen lost $0.000020 at $0.008917, marks were off $0.0005 at $0.5804, Swiss francs were $0.0010 lower at $0.6981, sterling was down $0.0006 at $1.6350, Canadian dollars were $0.0030 lower at $0.7230, Australian dollars were down $0.0012 at $0.7504 and Mexican pesos were $0.000425 higher at $0.121875.
